skill.name: megacave

content.user_title: Write Concise Technical Replies in Classical Chinese
content.value_statement: Verbose technical replies can slow reading for people comfortable with Classical Chinese. Megacave applies concise Classical Chinese phrasing while preserving technical details and clear safety explanations.
actual_capabilities: Directs chat replies into Classical Chinese with recoverable subjects omitted and classical particles connecting clauses.
Preserves code, commands, paths, API names, error strings, negations, numbers, and units without translation.
Maintains the response style until the user requests stop caveman or normal mode.
Uses plain Chinese or the user language for ambiguous clauses, confusion, security warnings, and irreversible-action confirmation.
Limits tool narration to short lines before and after runs, with exceptions for safety and harness requirements.
Excludes persisted artifacts from style compression, except for the named caveman-compress exception.
limitations: The skill provides response instructions, not an executable translator or a guaranteed enforcement mechanism.
Readers need familiarity with Classical Chinese; unclear clauses should use plain language.
Shorter displayed text does not guarantee lower token usage or lower costs.
Status reporting and command aliases depend on the host integration; this package contains no hook implementation.

use_cases.title: Read compact debugging explanations
use_cases.description: Receive concise Classical Chinese explanations while keeping API names, errors, and numeric details unchanged.

use_cases.title: Reduce narration during tool workflows
use_cases.description: Keep tool-run updates short while retaining clear warnings and confirmation requests for irreversible actions.

use_cases.title: Compare technical writing styles

prompt_templates.title: Explain a simple concept
prompt_templates.prompt: /megacave Explain why a connection pool reuses open connections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: try the style with one technical concept.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a rendering issue
prompt_templates.prompt: /megacave Explain why new object references can cause repeated rendering and when useMemo can help. Keep identifiers unchanged.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: preserve technical names while shortening an explanation.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize supplied diagnostics
prompt_templates.prompt: /megacave Summarize these diagnostics: [paste diagnostics]. Preserve errors, paths, numbers, units, and negations. Use plain language for ambiguous clauses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: condense evidence without losing operational details.

prompt_templates.title: Separate chat style from deliverables
prompt_templates.prompt: /megacave Review this proposed change: [paste change]. Keep chat concise, write persisted artifacts normally, and explain security concerns fully before irreversible actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: apply the style while protecting safety explanations and saved work.

best_practices: Activate the style explicitly and request normal mode when readability suffers.
Check that identifiers, negations, numbers, and units remain unchanged.
Keep security warnings, irreversible-action confirmations, and persisted artifacts in clear, ordinary language.
anti_patterns: Treating shorter displayed replies as guaranteed token or cost savings.
Translating API names, commands, paths, or errors to match the Classical Chinese style.
Compressing ambiguous instructions, security warnings, or saved documents into terse Classical Chinese.

faq.question: How do I activate megacave?
faq.answer: Use /megacave in Claude Code. The README also lists /caveman wenyan as an alias; availability depends on the host integration.

faq.question: How do I stop the style?
faq.answer: Say stop caveman or normal mode. The instructions otherwise keep the style active for the session.

faq.question: Does it reduce token costs?
faq.answer: No reliable savings are guaranteed. The README describes one small measurement and explicitly distinguishes shorter visible text from token reductions.

faq.question: Will technical identifiers be translated?
faq.answer: No. The instructions preserve code, commands, paths, API names, errors, numbers, units, and negations.

faq.question: Does it change saved documents or code?
faq.answer: The instructions exempt persisted artifacts from the style, including code, comments, commits, documentation, and messages. They name caveman-compress as an exception.

faq.question: What happens when brevity makes a reply unclear?
faq.answer: Ambiguous clauses use plain Chinese. Confusion, security warnings, and irreversible-action confirmation use full sentences in plain Chinese or the user language.
